observations: The actual Benares 1896 printing has 22 numbered entries. Asterisks and the exclamation mark on puroḍā are printed.
The shorter Kāśikā list and the Gaṇapāṭha grouped display have 14 and 21 head tokens with their own spellings.
Kāśikā puroha is paired with Vasu praroha. Gaṇapāṭha has the joined prarohasthā label.
Vasu pairs kṛṣi and ṛṣi. Kāśikā and Gaṇapāṭha actually list ṛṣi.
Vasu pairs viśikā and śibikā. Gaṇapāṭha has both viśikhā and viśikā; Kāśikā has śibikā.
Gaṇapāṭha carā differs from curā. Its paroḍā differs from questioned Vasu puroḍā.
Printed titikṣā is starred. Vācaspatyam explicitly confirms its named habitual ṇa derivative.
Vasu prints bhakṣā. Lexica attest bhākṣa and bhākṣī. Apte writes aṇ in his construction gloss.
The only named sthā examples here have the three specified prefixes. Nyāsa gives the prefixed reading of the bare roster label.
The nominal sources identify each prefixed base with the specific sthā and aṅ analysis.
The independently named baubhukṣa example fixes the gaṇa relation in the hunger head.
The general habitual-ṇa feminine inference and the positively named chātrī apply to the selected outputs.
Two pitch placements of pāraśvadhika are printed on the same page, in different words with the same segmental spelling.
The printed 4.4.59 rule and both examples directly retain long ī.
Vasu gives fate belief and separately allows belief restricted to what can be proved under daiṣṭika.
Print separates the 4.4.63 study error, the polysyllabic-first-member exception and the 4.4.65 dative question.
decisions: Bind each token to its exact roster and keep the 1896 collation independently citable.
Construct the four positively headed Vasu forms PR, TI, KR and BH on the applicable roster, with no cross-source promotion of praroha or kṛṣi into Kāśikā.
Supply the remaining Kāśikā operands onto the source-licensed habit query. Keep the known five earlier masculine fibres at their recorded credit.
Construct prefixed sthā forms through a preceding nominal operation. The bare label is a class shorthand.
Leave the compound-looking raw Gaṇapāṭha, carā, paroḍā, and the exact further conflicting entries as genuine open lexical evidence.
Treat habitual taitikṣa separately from the word and school histories listed under the separate head.
Use ṇa in the selected bhākṣa construction and retain Apte's aṇ label as an independent lexical source report.
Extend the justified habitual-ṇa ṅīp operation through the selected feminine addresses. Retain both prior dental spellings for the student.
Add direct print corroboration of the earlier pāraśvadhika accent pair.
Add direct print corroboration of the earlier long īkak masculine surface pair.
Keep both interpretations of daiṣṭika in the named printed explanation.
Keep study error and suitable food separate. Record the Vasu dative explanation for its exact phrase rather than transferring it to 4.4.62.
